solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He's keen to introduce part of lyric poem

indicators.note: the sharpening word comes first and leads in the pronoun after it

parts.note: to keen a blade is to sharpen it, as a strop does, so keen gives the verb strop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man eager to present an extract from a lyric poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' is a verb here, to sharpen, not eager. STROP leads in ('to introduce') HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophe is a stanza of a Greek choral ode, so a section of a lyric poem.

clue.text: Hack grabs page headline

indicators.note: grabs means the cutting word takes hold of the page letter inside

parts.note: to hack is to slash or cut roughly

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist seizes the front page story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist but is a verb, to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is the main front-page story, given the biggest headline in a newspaper.

clue.text: What top policeman did is nasty

parts.note: ran as in managed or ran a department, which is what the boss did
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch a senior officer heads

explanation.surface: The chief constable's conduct was disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as what the head of detectives did: ran CID, the British police's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid means rank or rotten-smelling, so broadly unpleasant or foul.

clue.text: One standing in for man or father

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: standing in means the numeral is placed inside the word for man

parts.note: a gent is a man
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A deputy acting on behalf of either the man or his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One standing in' looks like a deputy; it is I inside GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is an ancestor or parent, the one who begets offspring.

clue.text: City will accept most of this moral code

indicators.note: will accept means the City letters take in what follows

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: most of means the word this loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The financial district will adopt most of this set of principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims THIS to THI, which EC takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of principles governing right conduct, a moral system.

clue.text: Returning shots, posh girl's breaking ball

indicators.note: returning means both pieces that follow are read back to front

parts.note: nips are small shots of spirits
gel is the upper-class British pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: A well-bred girl's drinks being sent back cause trouble with a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns NIPS + GEL into LEGSPIN. In cricket a leg-break turns ('breaks') off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg-spin delivery deviates, or breaks, after pitching, a classic breaking ball.

clue.text: Dog runs around with ball — gets one swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means the phrase goes inside the laps-and-ball letters

parts.note: laps are circuits run around a track
gets one becomes has a
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: A dog chases round with a ball and gulps one down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets one' becomes HAS A, 'swallowed' by L-APSO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired breed of dog from Tibet.

clue.text: Digs using hook

definitions.meaning: digs is British slang for lodgings; slang for one's home
a hooked pole used to land large fish

explanation.surface: Excavating with a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaff is slang for a house or flat, and also a barbed fishing pole for landing a catch.

clue.text: A timer used primarily on bank alarms

parts.note: a as in a pound a head means per

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of timer and used are taken

parts.note: RBS is the Royal Bank of Scotland

explanation.surface: A time-lock device used to trigger bank alarms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means per, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to unsettle or disturb, much as alarming someone does.

clue.text: Picture file that is in sign, I am told

indicators.note: in means the file and abbreviation go inside the gesture word

parts.note: a nod is a sign of assent
TIF is a computer image file format

explanation.surface: Someone hears there is an image file contained within a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am' just links, as in I am notified.
explanation.definitionFit: Being notified means being informed or advised, which is being told something.

clue.text: Unfinished joint — leave tongue

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the joint word is dropped

parts.note: a link is a joint in a chain
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Abandoning a half-smoked joint, someone tells another to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the K from LINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language, and tongue is another word for a language.

clue.text: Recklessly smashed the fences around hollowed out trees

indicators.note: fences means the jumbled letters enclose what follows
smashed means the three letters of the word the are broken up and reordered
hollowed out means only the outer letters of around are kept

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: A careless driver crashes through fences around gutted trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' turns THE into HET, which 'fences' the rest; 'hollowed out' keeps only the outer letters of 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going headfirst means rushing in without thought, so rashly or recklessly.

clue.text: Seafood spread in crispbread

indicators.note: spread suggests something laid out and scattered, so the letters of crispbread are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish paste spread on a crispbread cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a paste on a cracker but signals the anagram of all ten letters of CRISPBREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The spider crab is an edible long-legged crustacean, a kind of shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Ducks out of tour of manor

indicators.note: out of means the ducks are removed from the words tour of

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O, so ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: Waterfowl escaping during a visit round a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manor' is British slang for one's own territory or patch, not a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf and manor are both slang for the area a gang or police officer controls.

clue.text: Impressed by famous son's opening kick in fight

indicators.note: opening means the son letter opens up the kick word and sits inside

parts.note: kick-start: to start is to give a kick to get going
a ruck is a brawl or fight

explanation.surface: A celebrity's son starts a brawl by kicking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kick' is to start (as in kick-start); 'opening' puts the son inside it, giving STARST.
explanation.definitionFit: Star-struck describes being dazzled by celebrities, impressed by the famous.

clue.text: Dodgy builder, 23, sacked

indicators.note: sacked as in ransacked, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the answer to clue 23 is PASTE

explanation.surface: A cowboy builder and his mate get fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' (as in plundered) rearranges BUILDER plus the answer to 23, PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disreputable has a poor reputation, so it is shady or dodgy.

clue.text: Conductor not on list

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor
off is the opposite of on

explanation.surface: A conductor is missing from the roster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle off is to recite a series quickly, as one would list items.

clue.text: Texan killer's blown cash in a week

indicators.note: blown as in money squandered, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A Texas murderer burns through his money in seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown' rearranges CASHINA to CHAINSA.
explanation.definitionFit: The film The Texas Chain Saw Massacre made this power tool a famous killer's weapon.

clue.text: Nobody keeps soldiers under cover

indicators.note: keeps means the insect word holds the soldiers inside

parts.note: an insect is a contemptibly insignificant person, a nobody
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An insignificant person hides troops secretly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly is doing it under cover, out of sight.

clue.text: Stuffed shirts may be so lined?

definitions.meaning: stuffed in the slang sense of beaten or left in the lurch
washed shirts are pegged on a clothes line

explanation.surface: Pompous people, like laundry, might be left dangling on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed shirts' reads as pompous people; split it, 'Stuffed' is one definition and the shirts on a washing line are the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abandoned to one's fate is being stuffed, and laundry pegged on a washing line hangs there.

clue.text: Note given to judge: Acquit

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: A message to the judge says to find the accused not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit oneself well is to make amends, the sense of redeem as discharge or atone.

clue.text: Stamp? A letter needs one on top

parts.note: em is the name of the letter M
a boss is the one in charge, on top

explanation.surface: Philately joke: a letter needs a postage stamp on the envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp?' suggests postage; it means press a raised design.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to stamp a raised pattern into paper or metal.

clue.text: I live in the mountains and I happen to get by

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place, as in so be it
by as in multiplication, times, written as the sign X

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller boasts of the chances of getting by.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the animal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of the Alps and other high ranges, so a mountain dweller.

clue.text: Closely follow cricketers, side securing runs

parts.note: slips are fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket

indicators.note: securing means the team word holds the runs letter inside it

parts.note: a side is a team
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders on a team that keeps scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: To slipstream is to follow right behind another vehicle to ride in its wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipstreaming means tailing closely behind a car or cyclist to benefit from reduced drag.

clue.text: Gum over top of envelope

parts.note: over means finished, past

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of envelope in this down clue

explanation.surface: Glue placed over the flap of an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is an adhesive, and paste is likewise a glue for sticking paper.

clue.text: One engineer not digging

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the three letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single engineer is not excavating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' is a verb rearranging NOT to NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Into is slang for keen on, and digging is old slang for liking.

clue.text: Not sure flabby American is energetic

indicators.note: flabby means slack and out of shape, so these letters lose their form

explanation.surface: Doubt whether an overweight American is really active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flabby' rearranges NOTSURE to STRENUO.
explanation.definitionFit: Strenuous effort is vigorous and demanding, much like energetic activity.

clue.text: River party finds plant blight

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Guests at a riverside party discover diseased plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a rust fungus stage that attacks plants, a form of plant disease.

clue.text: Reason trifle turns green?

parts.note: wit is intelligence or reason, as in at one's wits' end

indicators.note: turns means the dessert word is read backwards

parts.note: a trifle and a fool are both British cold desserts

explanation.surface: Wondering why a pudding goes mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' is a pudding, so FOOL (a fruit-and-cream dessert), which 'turns' to LOOF. The question mark flags a green as a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Witloof is chicory grown as a salad vegetable, the kind of leaf called greens.

clue.text: Northerners in English film with huge following

parts.note: a skim is a thin film on a liquid's surface
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A British movie that wins a big fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is a thin coating here, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit and related Arctic peoples were called Eskimos, inhabitants of the far north.
